answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring a ripple of sequential peer attestations that cannot be parallelized. Each dawn of the epoch, agents must fold fresh shared randomness into their prior interaction plume, generating unique traces that demand real sequential compute and one-to-one exchanges. Cloning a farm becomes costly because each fake identity must independently sustain its own ripple chain; attackers pay superlinear resources to maintain parallel histories that the network verifies against the shared plume of commitments.
